words.meaning: Long story books about people and events.

words.meaning: Written works such as stories, poems, and plays.

hard.funny_explanation: If a dog started playing the piano at the school talent show, it would be an absolute sensation!

examples.text: Sensation novels were designed to keep readers on the edge of their seats.
The new flavor of spicy ice cream caused a sensation, mostly because everyone’s tongue turned blue.

hard.real_world_analogy: A viral video that everyone is talking about the next morning at the bus stop.

words.meaning: Without any problems or hard work.
Ready for someone to use or buy.

medium.simple_explanation: Ready to be used or easy to get.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when the school cafeteria actually has pizza left when it's finally your turn in line.

examples.text: These translated books were easily available in local bookstores.
I am always available for a nap, no matter what time of day it is.

words.meaning: Written again in a different language.
More than two but not many.
The systems of speaking and writing.
relating to habits and beliefs of a group.
who or what a person or group is.
related to a country ruled by another.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a time when one powerful country controls and rules over another country.
medium.funny_explanation: Imagine if a giant neighbor moved into your house, changed all the TV channels, and told you what to eat for breakfast—that’s the 'colonial' vibe.

examples.text: The colonial government introduced many new laws to the region.
Living in a colonial era meant your boss lived thousands of miles away and didn't even know your name.

words.meaning: the state or quality of being modern.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe the transition from traditional Indian life to a world influenced by Western science and colonial rule.
hard.simple_explanation: The quality of being modern or having new ideas and technology.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like trading in your old bullock cart for a shiny, self-driving electric car with a built-in pizza oven.

examples.text: The characters in the novel struggled to balance tradition with the pull of modernity.
My grandfather embraces modernity by using his smartphone to watch videos of people making traditional pots.

hard.real_world_analogy: Modernity is like updating your computer's operating system; the core machine is the same, but everything looks and works differently now.

words.meaning: making someone feel afraid or scared.
too strong or attractive to be stopped.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes how colonial lifestyle and new technology were so attractive that characters couldn't say no to them.
hard.simple_explanation: Too attractive or tempting to be resisted.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a giant chocolate cake sitting on your desk while you're on a diet—that cake is irresistible!

examples.text: The allure of new Western gadgets was irresistible to the young men in the story.
The smell of fresh samosas is irresistible, even if I just finished a five-course meal.

hard.real_world_analogy: Irresistible is like a magnet pulling a paperclip; the paperclip has no choice but to go toward it.

words.meaning: having or showing good judgment.

medium.simple_explanation: Being practical and making smart, logical choices.
medium.funny_explanation: A sensible person is someone who brings an umbrella when it's cloudy, rather than hoping a giant leaf will fall from a tree to cover them.

examples.text: It is sensible to save money for things you might need later.
My cat is not very sensible; he thinks he can fight the vacuum cleaner and win.

words.meaning: having a lot of experience of life.

medium.simple_explanation: Having a lot of experience and understanding of how the world works.
medium.funny_explanation: This is like that one friend who knows exactly how to get a discount at every store and never gets lost in a big city.

examples.text: Traveling to different countries made her very worldly-wise.
The kitten acted worldly-wise until it saw its own reflection and did a backflip out of fear.

words.meaning: relating to doing things rather than ideas.
deeply connected to a place or culture.

medium.simple_explanation: Firmly connected to one's culture, family, or beliefs.
medium.funny_explanation: Being rooted means you're so connected to your traditions that even a hurricane of new trends can't knock you over.

examples.text: The author remained rooted in his traditional values despite moving abroad.
I am so rooted in my love for pizza that I refuse to admit other foods exist.

words.meaning: customs followed for a long time.
being worthy of honor or respect.

medium.simple_explanation: The quality of being worthy of respect and behaving in a calm, serious way.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s the art of walking away with your head held high even after you’ve accidentally tripped over a flat surface.

examples.text: She handled the difficult situation with great dignity.
My dog tries to maintain his dignity even when he’s wearing a ridiculous holiday sweater.

words.meaning: high respect or great pride.
trying to do something.
to connect two different things together.

medium.simple_explanation: To connect or bring together two different things or groups.
medium.funny_explanation: Metaphorically, it's like building a walkway between your love for video games and your need to pass history class.

examples.text: The new novel helped to bridge the gap between old and new cultures.
I tried to bridge the gap between my cat and the dog, but they just agreed to hate each other from a distance.

words.meaning: to make something modern or new.

medium.simple_explanation: To update something to make it current or use newer methods.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like taking your grandma’s rotary phone and trading it in for a smartphone that can order pizza by voice.

examples.text: The farmers decided to modernise their techniques to produce more food.
My dad tried to modernise his fashion sense, but he just ended up wearing neon socks with sandals.

words.meaning: the usual way of doing something.
passing on information or ideas.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book explains how Indian languages were adapted to pass on or 'transmit' Western knowledge.
hard.simple_explanation: Passing something from one place or person to another.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like playing a game of 'Chinese Whispers' but with science books instead of secrets.

examples.text: Newspapers were useful for transmitting information about social reforms.
The radio was transmitting strange sounds that my cat thought were messages from space.

hard.real_world_analogy: Transmitting is like a postman delivering letters; the language is the postman, and the knowledge is the letter.

words.meaning: knowledge gained through experience.
strongly encouraged to do something.

medium.simple_explanation: Strongly encouraged or persuaded to do something.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like when your mom tells you 'it would be a great idea' to clean your room, but her eyes say 'do it right now or else'.

examples.text: The teacher urged the students to start studying for the final exam early.
My stomach urged me to eat the third slice of cake, and I didn't want to be rude.

words.meaning: to develop a quality or skill.

medium.simple_explanation: To grow or develop a skill, habit, or quality through effort.
medium.funny_explanation: Like trying to cultivate the habit of waking up early—it requires a lot of 'planting' alarms and 'watering' yourself with coffee.

examples.text: He tried to cultivate a healthy habit of reading every single day.
I’m trying to cultivate a mysterious vibe, but I keep tripping over my own shoelaces.

words.meaning: something a person does often.
gives special importance to something.

medium.simple_explanation: To give special importance or attention to something.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like using a highlighter on a whole page because you think every single word is going to be on the test.

examples.text: The book emphasises that family values are the most important thing.
My brother emphasises his hunger by lying dramatically on the kitchen floor until he is fed.

words.meaning: giving up something valuable for a reason.

medium.simple_explanation: Giving up something important to achieve or keep something else.
medium.funny_explanation: Sacrificing is when you give up your precious sleep to finish a project you should have started a week ago.

examples.text: He succeeded in his career without sacrificing his personal principles.
I am sacrificing my dignity by wearing this giant chicken costume for the school play.

words.meaning: things that you plan to do.

medium.simple_explanation: A person's aims, plans, or reasons for doing something.
medium.funny_explanation: Good intentions are when you plan to do your chores, but then the internet happens and three hours disappear.

examples.text: Even with good intentions, the project did not turn out as expected.
The cat had good intentions when he brought me a dead bug; he just didn't realize I wasn't hungry.

words.meaning: giving advice about right and wrong behavior.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the critical feedback given to the novel 'Pariksha-Guru' for being too preachy about right and wrong.
hard.simple_explanation: Talking to people in a way that shows you think you are better or more 'correct' than they are.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a cartoon character with a halo constantly telling you to eat your broccoli and never, ever jump on the bed.

examples.text: Some readers found the novel's moralising tone quite boring.
I tried to watch a cartoon, but it was so moralising I felt like I was in a three-hour long lecture.

hard.real_world_analogy: Moralising is like a GPS that doesn't just tell you the turn, but judges you for taking the wrong way by sighing loudly.

words.meaning: very bright or impressive.
things that are not real or imagined.
to a very great degree.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize the huge impact the novel 'Chandrakanta' had on popularizing the Hindi language.
hard.simple_explanation: To a very great degree; extremely.
hard.funny_explanation: If a giant elephant sat on a tiny chair, the chair would be immensely crushed.

examples.text: The book was immensely popular among the educated classes of the 19th century.
I was immensely happy when I found an extra ten-rupee note in my old jeans.

hard.real_world_analogy: Immensely is like comparing the size of the Pacific Ocean to a puddle in your backyard.

words.meaning: making something liked by many people.

medium.simple_explanation: Making something liked or used by a large number of people.
medium.funny_explanation: It's what happens when one cool kid wears a weird hat, and by next week, the whole school looks like they're in a hat club.

examples.text: The author played a huge role in popularising the new language.
I am popularising the idea of eating dessert for breakfast, one donut at a time.

words.meaning: a system of writing.
according to what seems to be true.

medium.simple_explanation: Used to describe something that seems to be true based on what you can see or hear.
medium.funny_explanation: Apparently, if you don't charge your phone, it dies. Who would have guessed?

examples.text: The book was apparently written just for fun, but it has a deep meaning.
Apparently, the dog thinks the mailman is a supervillain trying to steal our junk mail.

words.meaning: deep understanding of a person or thing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text mentions that even entertainment novels provide deep understanding into what people feared or wanted.
hard.simple_explanation: A deep or clear understanding of a complicated person or situation.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like having X-ray goggles that let you see exactly why your friend is actually grumpy (spoiler: they missed lunch).

examples.text: The novel gives us insights into the social issues of the colonial era.
Studying the cat's behavior gave me insights into its master plan to take over the sofa.

hard.real_world_analogy: An insight is like finding the secret map in a video game that shows you where all the hidden treasures are.

words.meaning: strong feelings of wanting something.
the quality of being outstandingly good.
moved or changed position.
having the power to change things.

medium.simple_explanation: Having the power to change how others think or behave.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a YouTuber who mentions a specific snack and suddenly every store in the country is sold out of it.

examples.text: Premchand was an influential writer who changed Hindi literature forever.
My little sister is surprisingly influential; she convinced the whole family to have a tea party for her teddy bear.

words.meaning: people who judge or review work.

medium.simple_explanation: People who give professional opinions and judgments about books, movies, or art.
medium.funny_explanation: Professional 'I-don't-like-that' people, though sometimes they actually like things.

examples.text: Many critics praised the novel for its realistic portrayal of society.
The toughest critics of my cooking are my younger brothers, who prefer frozen nuggets to anything else.

words.meaning: a place where someone lives.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This word is part of the translated title of Premchand's novel, 'Sewasadan' (The Abode of Service).
hard.simple_explanation: A place of residence; a house or home.
hard.funny_explanation: A fancy, old-fashioned way to say 'the place where I keep my snacks and sleep.'

examples.text: The title 'The Abode of Service' reflects the novel's focus on social work.
Welcome to my humble abode, where the carpet is made of discarded socks.

hard.real_world_analogy: An abode is like a bird's nest—it's the specific safe spot where you live and rest.

words.meaning: a field or area of activity.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text explains how Premchand moved Hindi novels from the 'realm' of fantasy to reality.
hard.simple_explanation: A kingdom or a field of activity/interest.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as a 'level' in a game. Premchand moved the story from the 'Magic Dragon Realm' to the 'Real World Social Issues Realm.'

examples.text: The writer moved the novel from the realm of fantasy to serious social reflection.
In the realm of my bedroom, I am the king of messy blankets.

hard.real_world_analogy: A realm is like a specific department in a giant toy store—one for Barbies, one for Legos, one for Board Games.

words.meaning: things that people enjoy for fun.
serious thought about something.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that shows or represents the nature of something else.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your messy room is a reflection of your chaotic week—it’s a mirror showing the truth.

examples.text: The story was a serious reflection on the lives of ordinary people.
My hair in the morning is a perfect reflection of the crazy dreams I had.

words.meaning: normal or not special.
problems or topics for discussion.
property or money given at marriage.

medium.simple_explanation: Property or money brought by a bride to her husband's family on their marriage.
medium.funny_explanation: In the past, it was like a forced 'joining fee' paid in cows or gold just to get married.

examples.text: The novel discussed the social problems caused by the dowry system.
Imagine if instead of a dowry, families just traded rare trading cards at weddings.

words.meaning: mixed or linked together.

medium.simple_explanation: Closely connected or integrated into something, like threads in a cloth.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how the plot of a good movie is woven together so tightly you can't miss a minute without getting lost.

examples.text: Social issues were woven into the very fabric of the story.
The lie I told was so woven with other lies that I eventually forgot what the truth was.

words.meaning: chances to do something.
people in power or control.

medium.simple_explanation: The people or organizations that have the power to make decisions and enforce laws.
medium.funny_explanation: The people who wear the big hats and make the rules you have to follow, whether you like them or not.

examples.text: They had to ask the colonial authorities for permission to build the school.
I had to check with the household authorities (my parents) before inviting ten people over.

words.meaning: to rule or control a country.

medium.simple_explanation: To officially control and make decisions for a country, state, or group.
medium.funny_explanation: To be the boss of a whole place and deal with all the boring paperwork that comes with it.

examples.text: The local leaders wanted the right to govern themselves.
If I could govern the world, Mondays would be officially deleted from the calendar.

words.meaning: people sent to spread a religion.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: They are credited with writing the first novels in Assam to spread their message.
hard.simple_explanation: People sent on a religious mission, especially to promote Christianity in a foreign country.
hard.funny_explanation: They are like international cultural exchange students, but they come with books and a very specific religious goal.

examples.text: Missionaries were responsible for translating early Bengali works into Assamese.
The missionaries were so busy writing books that they probably forgot to pack their sunscreen.

hard.real_world_analogy: Missionaries are like brand ambassadors for a religion, traveling far away to tell people about their 'product' and way of life.

words.meaning: changing text into another language.
a magazine or daily record.
entering a place with an army.

hard.funny_explanation: It's like when your neighbors decide your backyard is actually theirs and move in with a giant tent and a drum set without asking.

The invasion of ants into the kitchen meant that my sugar bowl was now under new management.

hard.real_world_analogy: An invasion is like a computer virus that forces its way into your system to take control.

words.meaning: a planned set of military actions.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the military operations or 'campaign' that took place in 1819.
hard.simple_explanation: A series of military operations intended to achieve a goal.
hard.funny_explanation: A very organized, long-term plan—like a 'campaign' to convince your parents to get you a dog.

examples.text: Soldiers shared stories of the 1819 campaign with the author.
My summer campaign to eat every flavor of ice cream was a delicious success.

hard.real_world_analogy: A campaign is like a whole season of a sport, where you play many matches to win the final trophy.

words.meaning: a story about imaginary events.
very unfriendly or like an enemy.

hard.funny_explanation: The way two cats stare at each other through a window when they both want the same sunny spot.

I tried to be nice, but the grumpy old dog gave me a very hostile growl.

hard.real_world_analogy: Being hostile is like two rival sports teams before a big game—there's a lot of tension and nobody is sharing their water bottles.

words.meaning: kept away from each other.
coming together again after being apart.

hard.funny_explanation: Imagine you are wearing the latest sneakers while everyone else is in medieval boots; you are the contemporary fashion icon of the group.

examples.text: The museum features contemporary art pieces made by living artists.
My grandmother thinks using a smartphone is the most contemporary magic trick ever.

hard.real_world_analogy: A live news broadcast that tells you what is happening right this second compared to a history book about the dinosaurs.

words.meaning: Related to things that happened in the past.

words.meaning: Inside or closer to the center.

examples.text: They read novels about domestic issues like marriage and family.
I tried to have a domestic cat, but it acts more like a wild tiger that wants to eat my socks.

words.meaning: The place where something is positioned.

I’m the neighborhood candy merchant; I buy in bulk and sell for double the price at recess.

hard.funny_explanation: The kids who get the front row seats and the extra large slices of pizza just because they own the football.

hard.real_world_analogy: The VIP lounge at an airport where only a few people with special tickets get to sit in fancy chairs.

hard.funny_explanation: It’s like being the 'Official Sponsor' of your local ice cream shop by spending all your pocket money there every single day.

hard.real_world_analogy: A billionaire donating money to a library so they can buy new books and stay open.

hard.funny_explanation: A fancy party where people use their pinky fingers while drinking tea and talk about things like 'philosophy' instead of video games.

hard.real_world_analogy: A formal dinner party where everyone dresses up and acts very polite, unlike a wild birthday party at a trampoline park.

The contrast between my singing in the shower and my singing in music class is truly tragic.

words.meaning: Done by one person alone.

medium.simple_explanation: Carefully chosen as the best or most suitable from a group.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like being picked for the 'cool kids' table, but with fewer mean girls and more books.

examples.text: Only a select group of friends was invited to the book reading.
Only a select few can touch my secret stash of snacks without losing a finger.

words.meaning: All the people living in one house.

People who belong to a group.

Concerning books and pieces of writing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the friends and works associated with literature and intellectual reading.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to books and literature as an art form.
hard.funny_explanation: The difference between a text message that says 'k' and a 500-page novel about a lonely cloud.

examples.text: The professor had a vast knowledge of literary history and famous authors.
My brother tried to be literary by writing a poem about a burnt grilled cheese sandwich.

hard.real_world_analogy: A library filled with classic novels compared to a stack of comic strips.

words.meaning: To form an opinion about something.
Very surprised or shocked.

medium.simple_explanation: Very shocked or surprised.
medium.funny_explanation: The face you make when the teacher says 'Put your books away for a surprise test.'

examples.text: The audience was stunned by how quickly the Bengali novel became popular.
I was stunned to find out that 'fruit snacks' don’t actually count as eating a salad.

words.meaning: The quality of being extremely good.

hard.simple_explanation: Very clever, original, and inventive.
hard.funny_explanation: Using a vacuum cleaner to suck up a spider from across the room without touching it is an ingenious plan.

hard.real_world_analogy: A Swiss Army knife—one small tool that solves a dozen different problems in a clever way.

words.meaning: The main story of a book.

medium.simple_explanation: The main events of a story or the plan of a book.
medium.funny_explanation: The plot of my life is basically me walking into rooms and forgetting why I’m there.

examples.text: The novel had a plot full of exciting twists and turns.
My cat is definitely hatching a plot to take over the house and replace the dog.

words.meaning: Feeling excited or nervous about what happens next.

medium.simple_explanation: A feeling of excitement or anxiety about what might happen next.
medium.funny_explanation: Suspense is that moment when you’re waiting for the microwave to beep at 2 AM without waking up your parents.

examples.text: The suspense in the story kept the readers turning the pages.
The suspense of waiting for my crush to reply to 'Hey' is literally killing me.

words.meaning: Enjoyed something a great deal.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to show that readers greatly enjoyed the unique language and style of the new Bengali novels.
hard.simple_explanation: To enjoy something greatly; to savor an experience.
hard.funny_explanation: That look on your face when you take the first bite of a double-chocolate lava cake.

examples.text: She relished the opportunity to travel to the mountains for the first time.
The cat relished its victory after finally catching the elusive red laser dot.

hard.real_world_analogy: Slowly eating your favorite candy to make the taste last as long as possible.

hard.simple_explanation: Written or spoken language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure like poetry.
hard.funny_explanation: Regular talk. No rhyming, no dancing, just plain old words doing their jobs.

hard.real_world_analogy: A textbook or a newspaper article compared to a song lyrics or a rhyming nursery rhyme.

words.meaning: At the beginning or first.

hard.funny_explanation: Using words like 'gonna' and 'wanna' instead of 'I am going to' and 'I want to.'

examples.text: The book was written in a colloquial style to make the characters sound realistic.

hard.real_world_analogy: Talking to your best friend in your pajamas versus giving a speech to the President in a suit.

words.meaning: Connected with something else.

medium.simple_explanation: Connected with or linked to something else.

examples.text: The slang in the book was associated with urban life.
Rainy days are always associated with wanting to sleep for 48 hours straight.

words.meaning: Relating to a town or city.

examples.text: Many people moved to urban areas to find work in factories.
My dog is too 'urban' for the woods; he gets scared if there’s no sidewalk to walk on.

words.meaning: Took the place of something else.

hard.simple_explanation: Influenced by or made to conform to the rules and vocabulary of the ancient Sanskrit language.
hard.funny_explanation: Dressing up your regular sentences in a very fancy, royal tuxedo to make them look more important.

examples.text: The scholar used a Sanskritised version of the local language for his religious texts.
He tried to sound smart by using Sanskritised words, but he just ended up confusing the waiter.

hard.real_world_analogy: Adding very expensive and rare spices to a simple dish to make it taste like it’s from a 5-star restaurant.

words.meaning: The local language spoken by ordinary people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the common, local language that Bankim mixed with more formal styles.
hard.simple_explanation: The language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.
hard.funny_explanation: The special way people in your town talk that makes outsiders go, 'Wait, what did they just say?'

examples.text: The poet wrote in the vernacular so that the local villagers could enjoy his work.
My 'teenager vernacular' is basically a series of grunts that my parents somehow understand.

hard.real_world_analogy: Your local street food—it’s what the people actually eat and love every day, unlike fancy imported food.

words.meaning: A person in charge of a magazine or newspaper.

medium.simple_explanation: A person who decides what goes into a magazine or book and fixes the mistakes.
medium.funny_explanation: The person whose entire job is to tell a writer that they spelled 'the' wrong three times in one paragraph.

examples.text: As the editor of the magazine, he decided which stories to publish.
I wish I had an editor for my life who could delete all my embarrassing moments.

words.meaning: By a large number of people or everywhere.

medium.simple_explanation: By a large number of people or in many places.
medium.funny_explanation: Spreading like a loud sneeze in a very quiet library.

examples.text: The magazine was widely read by people all over the state.
It is widely known that my dog thinks he is a human.

words.meaning: Paper books published regularly with stories and news.
Easy to understand or do; not complicated.
The system of words used by people to speak.
Great bravery shown in a difficult situation.

medium.simple_explanation: Great bravery or courage.
medium.funny_explanation: Doing something super brave without looking back at the explosion, just like in the movies.

examples.text: The novel was full of stories of heroism and adventure.
My brother showed true heroism when he finally decided to clean his stinky room.

words.meaning: An exciting and unusual experience or journey.
A feeling of nervous excitement about what happens next.

medium.simple_explanation: A feeling of excited or nervous uncertainty about what may happen.
medium.funny_explanation: The feeling you get when your mom is scrolling through your phone's photo gallery and stops on a weird meme.

examples.text: The book was full of suspense, making it hard to stop reading.
The suspense of waiting for the pizza delivery guy is almost too much to handle.

words.meaning: Held the attention of someone by being interesting.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how Kalki's novels completely held the interest and attention of the Tamil-reading public.
hard.simple_explanation: To attract and hold someone's attention or interest strongly.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a giant magnet, but instead of pulling metal, it pulls your eyes and brain toward a juicy burger or a really cool video game.

examples.text: The magician captivated the audience with his incredible illusions.
The puppy captivated the entire family just by wagging its tail and tripping over its own ears.

hard.real_world_analogy: A bright lamp that makes a moth stop flying and just stare at it for hours.

words.meaning: People in general living in a community.
Including every part; the whole of something.
All the people born at the same time.

medium.simple_explanation: All of the people born and living at about the same time.
medium.funny_explanation: A group of people who all agree that their parents' music is old-fashioned.

examples.text: Kalki’s novels were loved by an entire generation of readers.
My generation is definitely the best at using emojis.

words.meaning: Published in a series of separate parts.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how the famous novel Ponniyin Selvan was published in parts in a magazine rather than all at once.
hard.simple_explanation: Published or broadcast in regular installments or parts.
hard.funny_explanation: It's the ultimate 'To Be Continued...' trick where the author gives you one slice of the pizza every week until you've finally eaten the whole thing.

examples.text: The story was serialised in the local newspaper over twelve weeks.
I wish my chores were serialised so I only had to clean one sock per day.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a TV show that releases one episode every Friday instead of letting you binge-watch the whole season.

words.meaning: People in a story, book, or movie.
Used words to communicate or tell a story.

medium.simple_explanation: Expressed thoughts or feelings to someone.
medium.funny_explanation: When a book talks to you without actually opening its mouth—it's a brain-to-brain connection.

examples.text: The novels spoke to their readers about the real problems of the world.
I tried to speak to my plant, but it just gave me the silent treatment.

words.meaning: To show or point out something clearly.

medium.simple_explanation: To show or point something out.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a GPS for social status, pointing out exactly where someone is from.

examples.text: The way characters spoke began to indicate which region they were from.
If I start yawning, it usually indicates that I am done with this homework.

words.meaning: A particular area or part of a country.
A social group based on birth in Hindu society.

medium.simple_explanation: A social group that people are born into, often with specific customs.
medium.funny_explanation: Like being sorted into a house at Hogwarts, but for real life and with a lot more historical rules.

examples.text: Novels showed the differences in language between various castes.
In the old days, your caste decided your job before you were even out of diapers.

words.meaning: Well known from being seen or heard before.
Pieces or sections of a larger whole.
A country or a specific area of ground.
Relating to the present or recent times.
Existing only in the mind; not real.
The earth and all people living on it.
The state of things as they actually exist.
A mental image of what might happen later.

medium.simple_explanation: A mental image of what the future could be like.
medium.funny_explanation: Putting on your 'What If?' goggles to see a world that hasn't happened yet.

examples.text: The author presented a vision of how the country ought to be.
I have a vision of a world where homework is illegal and pizza is free.

words.meaning: Relating to society or how people live together.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to how people live together in a society.
medium.funny_explanation: Dealing with the 'people' part of the planet—basically a giant group project that lasts forever.

examples.text: Social novelists often wrote about problems people faced in their daily lives.
I’m not being lazy; I’m just taking a break from my social responsibilities.

words.meaning: Satisfying one's idea of what is perfect.

medium.simple_explanation: Considered to be perfect or the best possible version.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'Instagram Filter' version of a person—perfect hair, perfect brain, and zero mistakes.

examples.text: The book described a hero with ideal qualities that everyone admired.
The ideal sandwich has exactly four layers of cheese and no crust.

words.meaning: Features or traits that make someone special.
To look at with respect and approval.
To copy the way someone looks or acts.

medium.simple_explanation: To copy the way someone else behaves or looks.
medium.funny_explanation: When you act exactly like your favorite movie star to look cool, or like your brother just to annoy him.

examples.text: Readers often wanted to imitate the brave heroes in the stories.
Stop trying to imitate my dance moves; you're making me look bad!

words.meaning: Explained the meaning of a word or idea.
Related to a country ruled by another country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the period when India was under British rule and the specific societal issues of that time.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a system where one country controls another country.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of a neighbor moving into your bedroom, eating your snacks, and making new rules for how you should brush your teeth.

examples.text: Colonial architecture can still be seen in many parts of Mumbai.
If cats ran a colonial empire, we would all be required to pay taxes in tuna.

hard.real_world_analogy: A guest who stays at your house but starts telling your parents what to cook for dinner.

words.meaning: A specific length of time in history.
In a way that achieves a good result.
Being the most important or main part.
Situations where a difficult choice is needed.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes the difficult choices people faced between following Western ideas or sticking to Indian traditions.
hard.simple_explanation: Situations where a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Brain Freeze' moment when you have enough money for one scoop of ice cream but can't decide between Chocolate and Strawberry.

examples.text: The student faced a dilemma: finish the essay or go to the football match.
My dog faces a daily dilemma: should he bark at the mailman or keep napping in the sun?

hard.real_world_analogy: Standing at a crossroads where both paths look equally interesting, but you can only walk down one.

words.meaning: People living under the rule of a government.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the people living under the authority of a colonial government.
hard.simple_explanation: People who live under the rule of a particular king, queen, or government.
hard.funny_explanation: In the kingdom of the classroom, the students are the subjects and the teacher is the wise (but sometimes strict) monarch.

examples.text: The British subjects were required to follow the laws of the Crown.
The subjects of the Great Cat Empire were mostly mice who were very, very nervous.

hard.real_world_analogy: Players in a board game who must follow the rules written by the game creator.

words.meaning: Refusing to accept or believe in something.

medium.simple_explanation: Refusing to accept or believe in something.
medium.funny_explanation: Taking an idea, putting it in the 'trash' bin of your mind, and clicking 'empty.'

examples.text: The characters were modern without rejecting their own traditions.
I am officially rejecting the idea that I have to wake up before 10 AM.

words.meaning: Beliefs or customs passed down through generations.

medium.simple_explanation: A custom or belief that has been passed down for a long time.
medium.funny_explanation: Things we do because our great-great-grandparents did them, and we don't want to be the ones to break the streak.

examples.text: It was important for people to keep their tradition while learning new things.
Our family tradition is to argue for an hour about which movie to watch.

words.meaning: Who a person is or what they represent.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the sense of who a person is and the fear of losing one's culture to Western influences.
hard.simple_explanation: The qualities, beliefs, and personality that make a person or group who they are.
hard.funny_explanation: It's your personal 'brand'—the unique mix of your favorite color, your weird laugh, and your love for spicy chips.

examples.text: The characters in the novel struggled to keep their cultural identity in a foreign land.
Superman has a secret identity so people don't ask him to help move heavy furniture every weekend.

hard.real_world_analogy: A fingerprint. No matter where you go, it stays the same and proves exactly who you are.

words.meaning: Showed or described someone in a certain way.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how the author Chandu Menon represented the character Indulekha in his writing.
hard.simple_explanation: Described or showed someone or something in a particular way.
hard.funny_explanation: Like using a filter on your photo to make yourself look like a glowing superhero or a mysterious vampire.

examples.text: The actor portrayed the king as a kind and generous leader.
The cartoon portrayed the rabbit as a genius, while the hunter was shown as a total goofball.

hard.real_world_analogy: A painting of a person. The artist chooses which colors and expressions to use to show the world who that person is.

words.meaning: Extremely beautiful, exciting, or surprising.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the extreme and impressive beauty of the character Indulekha.
hard.simple_explanation: So surprising, impressive, or beautiful that it could take your breath away.
hard.funny_explanation: The feeling you get when you see a triple-decker chocolate cake or a goal scored from the halfway line.

examples.text: The view from the top of the mountain was absolutely breathtaking.
The amount of laundry in my room is truly breathtaking, and not in a good way!

hard.real_world_analogy: That 'Gasp!' sound people make when they see something incredibly cool, like a shooting star.

words.meaning: Relating to the ability to think and understand.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes Indulekha’s mental strength and her ability to think and learn deeply.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to the ability to think in a logical way and understand difficult ideas.
hard.funny_explanation: Being a 'Smarty-Pants' who actually enjoys solving complex riddles and reading big books for fun.

examples.text: She possessed great intellectual curiosity and was always asking questions.
My dog thinks he’s an intellectual because he stares at the newspaper before chewing it up.

hard.real_world_analogy: The processor of a computer—it's the part that does all the heavy thinking and problem solving.

words.meaning: The power or skill to do something.
A natural skill or ability to do something.

medium.simple_explanation: A natural skill or ability to do something well.
medium.funny_explanation: A special 'cheat code' you were born with for things like singing, drawing, or eating pizza really fast.

examples.text: Indulekha was described as having a lot of artistic talent.
I have a hidden talent for falling asleep in places I shouldn't.

words.meaning: The process of learning at school or college.
An ancient language used in Indian literature.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Mentions the language Indulekha was educated in, showing her traditional side alongside her English education.
hard.simple_explanation: An ancient Indo-Aryan language that is the classical language of India and Hinduism.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Great-Grandfather' of many Indian languages. It’s very old, very precise, and very fancy.

examples.text: Many ancient Indian scriptures are written in Sanskrit.
I tried to learn a Sanskrit shloka, but my tongue felt like it was doing gymnastics.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like Latin in Europe, it is a root language that connects many different modern languages together.

words.meaning: A person who belongs to a specific group.
Taught or learned in the English language.

medium.simple_explanation: Having received an education in schools that use the English language.
medium.funny_explanation: People who can read Shakespeare and talk about science in English, hopefully without sounding too much like a dictionary.

examples.text: Madhavan belonged to the newly English-educated class of students.
He’s so English-educated that he actually knows how to use the word 'whom' correctly.

words.meaning: Long stories written about imaginary people and events.

medium.simple_explanation: Long storybooks that tell a fictional tale about people and events.
medium.funny_explanation: A book so long that by the time you finish it, you might be a year older and need a snack.

examples.text: Many people enjoy reading historical novels to learn about the past.
I tried to write a novel, but I ran out of ideas after two pages and a sandwich.

words.meaning: A large group of people living together.

medium.simple_explanation: A large group of people living together in an organized way.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically a giant group project where everyone lives in the same area and tries not to be too annoying.

examples.text: The novel reflected the changes happening in Indian society.
In a society of squirrels, the person with the most nuts is king.

words.meaning: The study of things that happened in the past.
The outside part of a book or magazine.
A thin book with stories, news, and pictures.

medium.simple_explanation: A thin book with a paper cover that comes out regularly with stories and pictures.
medium.funny_explanation: A book that's basically a snack for your brain—quick, colorful, and full of variety.

examples.text: Kathanjali was a popular magazine that published short stories.
I only read the sports magazine for the pictures of people falling down.

words.meaning: The act of printing a book for the public.

medium.simple_explanation: The act of printing a book or magazine and making it available to the public.
medium.funny_explanation: The moment a writer's secret diary or story finally escapes the house and meets the world.

examples.text: The publication of the new book caused a lot of excitement.
My publication of 'How to Sleep in Class' was rejected by the school newspaper.

words.meaning: Happening again and again at the same time.
A person who has deep knowledge about a subject.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this word to highlight the high intellectual status and deep traditional education of the male character who also adopted Western styles.
hard.simple_explanation: A person who has studied a subject for a long time and knows a lot about it.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of a scholar as a human Google search, but for books. They probably have more ink in their veins than blood and can talk about ancient history for five hours without blinking.

examples.text: He was a first-rate Sanskrit scholar who knew all the ancient texts by heart.
My little brother thinks he’s a dinosaur scholar just because he can name three T-Rexes and a chicken.

hard.real_world_analogy: A scholar is like a master chef who knows every single ingredient in a giant kitchen, whereas everyone else is just trying not to burn toast.

words.meaning: Related to countries like Europe and North America.
A bunch of hair or grass growing together.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the specific physical appearance of a character to show the mix of Western clothing and traditional Indian hairstyle.
hard.simple_explanation: A small bunch of hair, feathers, or grass growing close together.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a tiny, lonely island of hair that refuses to hang out with the rest of the hair on your head.

examples.text: He kept a long tuft of hair at the back of his head according to his custom.
The baby had a single tuft of hair that stood straight up whenever he saw a cookie.

hard.real_world_analogy: A tuft is like a single patch of grass sticking up in the middle of a perfectly flat sidewalk.

words.meaning: A traditional way of behaving in a group.

medium.simple_explanation: A traditional way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a group of people.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'unwritten rules' your family or country follows, like eating pizza with a fork or always wearing lucky socks.

examples.text: He kept a long tuft of hair according to the local custom.
In our house, it’s a custom for the dog to get the first bite of every pizza.

words.meaning: The main brave male characters in a story.
The main brave female characters in a story.

medium.simple_explanation: The main female characters in a story who are admired for their courage or good qualities.
medium.funny_explanation: The girls in the story who actually get things done while the hero is probably still tying his shoes.

examples.text: The heroines in modern novels were very different from those in old poems.
My favorite heroines are the ones who can save the world and still find time for snacks.

words.meaning: Relating to the present or recent times.
The best or most perfect possible thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Representing the best possible version of something; perfect.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a pizza with zero calories that tastes like heaven—basically, the dream version.

examples.text: She was looking for an ideal combination of traditional and modern ways.
My ideal morning involves a robot doing my homework while I stay in bed.

words.meaning: Based on ancient stories about gods and heroes.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text contrasts new, realistic novel characters with the magical or legendary characters found in older Indian literature.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to old stories about gods, heroes, and magic that aren't based on real-life facts.
hard.funny_explanation: Characters who can lift mountains with one finger and fly on giant birds. They are the original superheroes, but with cooler costumes and way more drama.

examples.text: Early Indian literature was filled with mythological characters and epic battles.
My excuse for the broken vase was a mythological dragon, but my mom didn't buy it.

hard.real_world_analogy: Mythological stories are like the Avengers movies of the ancient world—everyone knew the heroes, but nobody expected to see them at the grocery store.

words.meaning: The people that a story is about.

medium.simple_explanation: The people, animals, or creatures that play a part in a story.
medium.funny_explanation: The imaginary people living in a book who often have way more dramatic lives than we do.

examples.text: The characters in the book felt very realistic to the readers.
I like book characters who make bad decisions because it makes me feel better about mine.

words.meaning: Written works like novels, poems, and plays.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the entire body of written work in India, including poems and novels, that shaped society.
hard.simple_explanation: Books, poems, and plays that are considered to have lasting value and artistic merit.
hard.funny_explanation: The fancy way of saying 'the stuff people wrote down that’s actually good enough to be in a library.'

examples.text: The novel was a major change from the poetic literature of the past.
I tried to argue that my grocery list was modern literature, but my teacher disagreed.

hard.real_world_analogy: Literature is like a massive time-capsule filled with the best stories and thoughts of everyone who lived before us.

words.meaning: Relating to a country controlled by another power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the historical period when India was governed by Britain, which influenced how people lived and thought.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to a system where one country controls and rules over another country.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a neighbor moving into your living room, changing the TV channel, and telling you what time to eat dinner. That’s the vibe.

examples.text: Colonial rule introduced many Western ideas and lifestyles to the Indian middle class.
The cats established a colonial government in my bedroom, and now I have to pay rent in treats.

hard.real_world_analogy: It is like a big school bully deciding which games everyone else is allowed to play on the playground.

words.meaning: To have power and control over a country.
Something that is pleasing or nice to look at.
Felt afraid that something bad might happen.
Doing something completely or in a large way.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the fear of Indians completely and mindlessly accepting all Western values without keeping their own.
hard.simple_explanation: Doing something completely or on a very large scale.
hard.funny_explanation: When you don't just buy one chocolate bar, you buy the whole factory and the truck that delivered it.

examples.text: They feared that a wholesale adoption of foreign values would ruin their traditions.
The dog made a wholesale mess of the kitchen in under thirty seconds.

hard.real_world_analogy: Wholesale is like deciding to paint your entire house bright pink instead of just testing a small spot behind the door.

words.meaning: Starting to use or follow a new idea.

medium.simple_explanation: The act of starting to use or follow a new idea, habit, or way of doing things.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you suddenly decide you're a 'skater' and start carrying a board everywhere, even if you can't balance.

examples.text: The adoption of Western values worried some traditional families.
My cat's adoption of the laptop as his personal bed was quite sudden.

words.meaning: Beliefs about what is important or right.

medium.simple_explanation: The beliefs and principles that a person or group thinks are important.
medium.funny_explanation: The rules in your head that tell you lying is bad, but stealing a fry from your friend is... maybe okay.

examples.text: People feared that new values would destroy their old way of life.
My personal values include never waking up before 10 AM on a Saturday.

words.meaning: Following ways that have existed for a long time.

medium.simple_explanation: Following ideas or methods that have existed for a long time.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'old school' way of doing things, like using an actual map instead of GPS.

examples.text: They wanted to keep their traditional ways of living alive.
My grandma has a traditional way of making tea that takes three hours but tastes like magic.

words.meaning: Coming from a country that is not yours.
The way people choose to live their lives.

medium.simple_explanation: The different ways that people or groups live their lives.
medium.funny_explanation: The specific blend of what you eat, how you dress, and how much you binge-watch shows.

examples.text: The novel showed how different lifestyles could be brought together.
My lifestyle currently consists of 10% studying and 90% looking for my charger.

words.meaning: Two or more things joined or mixed together.

medium.simple_explanation: The result of mixing two or more things together.
medium.funny_explanation: Like putting fries inside a burger—it shouldn't be that good, but it is.

examples.text: The character represented an ideal combination of two cultures.
A combination of orange juice and toothpaste is a mistake you only make once.

words.meaning: Things that give a person joy or happiness.
Liked or enjoyed by a large number of people.
A way or method of doing something.

medium.simple_explanation: A way or method used to communicate or express something.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'vessel' for your message, whether it's a book, a TikTok, or a carrier pigeon.

examples.text: The novel became a popular medium of entertainment.
Screaming into a pillow is my favorite medium for expressing frustration.

words.meaning: Things like books that provide fun.

medium.simple_explanation: Things like movies, books, or games that people enjoy for fun.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything that stops you from staring at a wall and feeling bored.

examples.text: Novels provided a new form of entertainment for the middle class.
Watching my brother try to dance is the best entertainment I know.

words.meaning: The number of copies of a book sold.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It explains how printed books moved through society and reached many different people.
hard.simple_explanation: The movement or distribution of something from one person or place to another.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as a book’s world tour. It starts at the printer and ends up in everyone's hands, traveling faster than a secret in a school hallway.

examples.text: The circulation of printed books allowed more people to enjoy reading.
The circulation of the flu in our classroom was faster than the Wi-Fi.

hard.real_world_analogy: Circulation is like the blood moving through your body to reach your toes, but with books moving through a city to reach readers.

words.meaning: To keep someone interested and happy.
Changing words from one language to another.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text mentions that reading became popular because stories from other languages were rewritten into local languages.
hard.simple_explanation: The process of changing words from one language into another.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a magical language-swapping machine that lets you understand what someone halfway across the world is thinking.

examples.text: Translations of European novels were very popular among Indian readers.
My translation of my dog's bark is usually just 'Hey! Look! A squirrel!'

hard.real_world_analogy: A translation is like a cover song; the melody is the same, but the singer and the style might be totally different.

words.meaning: Made or written, like a song or poem.

medium.simple_explanation: Created or written, especially music, poetry, or stories.
medium.funny_explanation: When you carefully put words or notes together instead of just smashing the keyboard.

examples.text: Popular songs were sometimes composed to talk about current events.
I composed a beautiful poem about how much I hate broccoli.

words.meaning: Happening or existing at the same time.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to songs or stories that were written about things happening 'right now' in that time period.
hard.simple_explanation: Living or occurring at the same time; modern or current.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'now' stuff. If it’s on your social media feed today, it’s contemporary. If it's in a dusty museum, it’s not.

examples.text: Popular songs were often composed based on contemporary events.
My grandmother thinks contemporary fashion looks like we all got dressed in the dark.

hard.real_world_analogy: Contemporary is like the latest iPhone model, whereas historical is the old rotary phone that lived on your great-grandma’s wall.

words.meaning: Things that happen, especially important ones.
The habits and beliefs of a group.

medium.simple_explanation: The habits, beliefs, and art of a particular group of people.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'vibe' of a whole group of people, including their food, music, and how they celebrate.

examples.text: The new culture of print made novels very popular.
In the culture of my friend group, wearing mismatched socks is mandatory.

words.meaning: To a very great or large degree.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this word to show just how much people loved reading novels during the early 20th century.
hard.simple_explanation: To a very great or huge degree.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine the biggest, most giant pile of ice cream ever. That’s how much you 'immensely' like it.

examples.text: Novels became immensely popular within a short period of time.
I was immensely relieved when I realized it was Saturday and not Monday morning.

hard.real_world_analogy: It’s the difference between a tiny candle flame and a massive, roaring bonfire.

words.meaning: A very large amount of something appearing quickly.
Periods of ten years.

medium.simple_explanation: Periods of ten years.
medium.funny_explanation: A unit of time long enough for your parents' clothes to go from 'cool' to 'lame' to 'cool' again.

examples.text: It took several decades for the novel to become widely popular.
I feel like I've been waiting decades for this pizza to arrive.

words.meaning: Stories about solving crimes and finding clues.

medium.simple_explanation: Related to stories where someone tries to solve a crime or mystery.
medium.funny_explanation: The person in the book who notices a tiny piece of lint and somehow figures out who stole the diamonds.

examples.text: Detective novels were very popular and had to be printed many times.
I played detective to find out who ate the last cookie, but the crumbs on my face gave me away.

words.meaning: Something that is strange and hard to understand.

medium.simple_explanation: A story about a puzzling crime or situation that needs to be solved.
medium.funny_explanation: A book that keeps you guessing until the end, like trying to figure out where your left shoe went.

examples.text: Readers loved the suspense in mystery novels.
The greatest mystery of my life is why I’m always hungry five minutes after lunch.

words.meaning: The need or desire of people for something.

medium.simple_explanation: The desire of many people to have or buy something.
medium.funny_explanation: When everyone wants the same thing at once, like the last slice of pizza at a party.

examples.text: The demand for novels was so high that they were reprinted often.
There is a high demand for my autograph, mostly from people wanting me to sign their library fines.

words.meaning: Printed again to produce more copies.

medium.simple_explanation: When a book is printed again because all the previous copies were sold.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a movie sequel, but for a book that was so good everyone bought it the first time.

examples.text: Some popular books were reprinted twenty-two times!
My drawing was so bad that it definitely won't be reprinted in the yearbook.

words.meaning: Helped someone to do a task.

medium.simple_explanation: Gave help or support to someone or something.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your friend holds the ladder while you try to reach the top shelf—they're helping you not fall.

examples.text: The novel assisted in the spread of silent reading habits.
I assisted my mom by eating the cake she spent three hours baking.

hard.funny_explanation: A professional time-traveler who doesn't use a machine, but uses dusty old books and broken pots to solve mysteries from a thousand years ago.

examples.text: The historian discovered a new diary that explained the causes of the war.
I became a family historian by finding my dad's embarrassing 8th-grade report card.

hard.real_world_analogy: A detective who arrives at a crime scene 500 years late and still manages to figure out what happened.

words.meaning: Found the place where something is.

medium.simple_explanation: Found the exact position or place of something.
medium.funny_explanation: What you do after ten minutes of frantic searching when your phone was in your hand the whole time.

examples.text: The historian located two old novels in the ruins.
I finally located the source of the smell; it was a three-week-old pizza slice under my bed.

words.meaning: The period from the years 1901 to 2000.

medium.simple_explanation: The period of time from the year 1901 to 2000.
medium.funny_explanation: The century that gave us the moon landing, the internet, and those weird neon tracksuits our parents used to wear.

examples.text: The twentieth century saw the rise of global movies and TV.
In the year 3035, historians will think the twentieth century was when humans first learned to use a mouse.

words.meaning: Traditional ways of doing things in society.

medium.simple_explanation: Traditional ways of behaving or doing things that are specific to a particular society.
medium.funny_explanation: The weird things your family does, like having to eat certain foods on Tuesdays just because Grandma said so.

examples.text: The novel describes the local customs of the village.
It is one of our customs to pretend we like Auntie's dry fruitcake every Christmas.

words.meaning: To talk or write about something in detail.
The period from the years 1801 to 1900.

medium.simple_explanation: The period of time from the year 1801 to 1900.
medium.funny_explanation: A time of steam engines and very dramatic letters written with fancy ink, before anyone could just send a 'u up?' text.

examples.text: Many great writers lived in nineteenth-century Britain.
People in the nineteenth-century had way too much free time if they could read 800-page books by candlelight.

words.meaning: To give a short version of main ideas.

medium.simple_explanation: To give a brief statement of the main points of something.
medium.funny_explanation: Explaining a three-hour movie to your friend in ten seconds so they don't fall asleep.

examples.text: Summarise the main reasons why people were worried about women reading.
Can you summarise your excuse for not doing your homework in one sentence?

words.meaning: A feeling of worry about something.

medium.simple_explanation: A feeling of worry or interest about a particular situation.
medium.funny_explanation: The feeling you get when you see your teacher holding a stack of graded tests and they look disappointed.

examples.text: There was a growing concern about the influence of novels on young readers.
My only concern right now is how to eat this pizza without getting sauce on my white shirt.

words.meaning: To mention an idea for people to think about.
Looked at or thought of in a way.
A large country located in South Asia.
Helping someone to do or get something.
People who want political independence for their country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It identifies the group of people who used literature to promote the idea of a free and united India.
hard.simple_explanation: People who strongly identify with their nation and support its interests and independence.
hard.funny_explanation: The ultimate cheerleaders for their country, wearing the national flag as a cape and dreaming of independence all day.

examples.text: The nationalists used novels to inspire people to join the freedom struggle.
Even during the school football match, the nationalists in our class wore the school colors with pride.

hard.real_world_analogy: Fans at a stadium who only cheer for their own team and want them to win the championship more than anything.

words.meaning: To say what someone or something is like.
An important topic or problem to talk about.
A system of dividing society into social groups.

medium.simple_explanation: A social system that divides people into groups based on their birth.
medium.funny_explanation: An old-school, very unfair 'Sorting Hat' that decided your whole life before you even learned to walk.

examples.text: Indian novelists often wrote about the problems caused by the caste system.
I wish there was a caste for people who are professional nappers, because I would be the king.

words.meaning: Made something a part of a larger group.
Mentioning or talking about a specific thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Mentioning or talking about someone or something.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you say 'that person over there' while trying not to point with your finger.

examples.text: By referring to the textbook, you can find the answers.
When my mom says 'we need to talk,' she's usually referring to the mess in my room.

words.meaning: Something that is present or real now.

medium.simple_explanation: Present or real at the current time.
medium.funny_explanation: Something that is actually here, like the homework on your desk, even if you wish it would disappear.

examples.text: The author wanted people to think about existing social issues.
I'm currently existing on a diet of chips and chocolate.

words.meaning: Important problems that people talk about.
Tried to do something, often something difficult.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the effort made by novelists to create a common identity through their writing.
hard.simple_explanation: To make an effort to do something, especially something difficult.
hard.funny_explanation: The word for when you try to do something cool, like a backflip, and the book records the effort whether you landed it or not.

examples.text: The author attempted to bridge the gap between different cultures.
I attempted to bake a cake, but it ended up looking more like a very flat pancake.

hard.real_world_analogy: Taking a swing at a baseball; even if you miss, you still put in the work to hit it.

words.meaning: To make something new happen or exist.
A feeling or understanding of something.

medium.simple_explanation: A general feeling, understanding, or awareness of something.
medium.funny_explanation: That 'vibe' you get when you walk into a room and realize everyone was just talking about you.

examples.text: The novel helped create a sense of belonging among all Indians.
I have a strong sense that there is a donut somewhere in this house, and I will find it.

words.meaning: Relating to or including all parts of India.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The word explains the goal of creating a shared identity that covers all of India, not just specific regions.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to or representing the whole of India.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a giant umbrella that is big enough to cover every single person in India, from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.

examples.text: The novel helped create a pan-Indian sense of unity among the readers.
We had a pan-Indian lunch where we served butter chicken, idli, and dhokla on one plate.

hard.real_world_analogy: A mega-playlist that includes a favorite song from every single state in the country.

words.meaning: A feeling of being part of a group.
Belonging to the same time or modern times.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It is part of the book's title, referring to the world as it is in the present day or recent history.
hard.simple_explanation: Belonging to the same time or the present period.
hard.funny_explanation: Basically a fancy word for 'happening right now' or 'cool and modern,' like the latest viral dance move.

examples.text: Contemporary history focuses on events that have happened in our recent past.
My grandma's taste in music isn't exactly contemporary; she still loves her old record player.

hard.real_world_analogy: The 'Latest News' section of a website compared to the 'Archives' section.
